definition: Simple Variations on Arithmetic Math word Problems is a challenge set to enable more robust evaluation of automatic MWP (Math Word Problem) solvers
details: Simple Variations on Arithmetic Math word Problems is a challenge set to enable more robust evaluation of automatic MWP (Math Word Problem) solvers

explainer.lead: SVAMP is a challenge set of simple variations on arithmetic math word problems, built to test automatic solvers more robustly. It matters because it exposes solvers that pass standard benchmarks without genuinely reasoning.

tiers.eli5: It's a set of math word problems with small twists, to check whether a program really understands the problem or just memorized the usual wording.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use SVAMP to stress-test math word problem solvers beyond standard benchmarks. A pitfall is reading strong benchmark scores as robust reasoning when simple variations break them.
tiers.paperLevel: Simple Variations on Arithmetic Math word Problems, a challenge set enabling more robust evaluation of automatic MWP solvers. It targets arithmetic word problems specifically.

explainer.example: Taking a familiar arithmetic word problem and varying it slightly to see whether a solver still gets it right.
